reuse.why: isFixedGroup re-implements tag parsing with its own regex (with a comment asking to keep it in step) instead of calling the existing extractTagsFromText in shared/tags.ts, and no shared category-selection helper is introduced for the month-wide actions to reuse.

duplication.why: The saved-template SQL predicate is pasted into six queries, the hidden/group-hidden filter is written once as an SQL parameter trick in four queries and as JS conditions in two, and the whole category query plus loop is copied again for setLastMonthSpending.

placement.why: Everything stays in server/budget/actions.ts with the new handler registered in budget/app.ts next to its siblings, matching the tree's layering, though the exclusion rule is split between SQL and JS.

scope.why: Changes are limited to the four requested behaviours, the new handler registration and tests.

maintainability.why: Which categories a month-wide action writes is now decided in six places in three different shapes (SQL WHERE, SQL CASE column, JS ifs), so every further rule change has to be repeated at each action, as each step of this packet already did.

bypasses_abstraction.where: isFixedGroup in server/budget/actions.ts hand-rolls #tag matching instead of using extractTagsFromText from shared/tags.ts.

disguised_duplication.where: The hidden rule is expressed as `(? = 1 OR (c.hidden = 0 AND g.hidden = 0))` in the set3/6/12MonthAvg and setLastMonthSpending queries but as `!includeHiddenCategories && (hidden === 1 || group_hidden === 1)` in copyPreviousMonth and setZero; the saved-template rule appears both as a CASE column (getBudgetData, setZero) and as a NOT(...) WHERE clause (four queries).

abstraction_drift.where: No shared selection for month-wide categories exists or is created: copyPreviousMonth, setZero, setLastMonthSpending, set3MonthAvg, set6MonthAvg and set12MonthAvg each re-implement the hidden, saved-template and #fixed exclusions themselves, and isFixedGroup bypasses the shared tag parser.
